label_paper_title: Artificial Intelligence and Economic Growth
rationale: Questions and assumptions are explicit; reasoning is coherent and transparent. Models are clearly laid out; conclusions match derivations. Writing is accessible and effective for economists and policymakers. Minor reliance on stylized setups does not detract from clarity.

label_paper_title: Artificial Intelligence and Economic Growth
rationale: No replication package or code provided; uses public data sources but limited documentation for simulations. Methods are reproducible in principle for theory but empirical sections are not turnkey. Not preregistered; no multiple-testing issues relevant.

label_paper_title: Artificial Intelligence and Economic Growth
rationale: Addresses globally salient topics: AI’s effects on growth, labor shares, inequality, market structure. Policy implications (competition, IP, organization) are discussed, though quantification is limited and LMIC-specific analysis is brief. High relevance for priority-setting and foresight.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Overall reflects the mean across categories. Strong saturation-RCT design, clear empirical results, and policy relevance. Credibility is high but tempered by some measurement limitations (imprecise denominators in a subset of villages, retrospective employer outcomes), limited multiple-testing adjustments, and external-validity concerns given later mixed scale-up evidence.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Main claims—subsidies raise migration; spillovers increase village wages/hours; limited food price effects—are well supported by a saturation RCT, strong first stages, high-frequency household data, and employer/price surveys. Some secondary claims (employer profits, specific prices) are weaker due to retrospective measures and imprecise denominators in some villages. External validity is cautioned.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Well-justified saturation design enabling GE identification; IV with strong first stages; high-frequency measurement reduces recall bias; clustered SEs; checks on spatial spillovers. Assumptions (closed labor markets, short-run technology rigidity) are reasonable but not airtight. Limited multiple-hypothesis adjustments and some retrospective modules reduce robustness.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Provides rare experimental evidence on GE spillovers of internal migration, documenting wage, labor-supply, and distributional effects. Influential for debates on mobility policies and program scale-up. Incremental relative to more recent GE work and context-specific; later mixed results at scale temper field-wide impact.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Clear questions and theory organizing empirics; transparent assumptions; consistent logic from first stage to GE outcomes; coherent triangulation across HF surveys, endline, employers, and prices. Tables/labels are clear; limitations acknowledged.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Pre-registered (AEA RCT registry 2507) with disclosures and substantial design detail. Public data/code availability is unclear; complex implementation may hinder easy reproduction; limited explicit multiple-testing plans. Better than average pre-2019 standards, below current best practices.

label_paper_title: Effects of Emigration on Rural Labor Markets
rationale: Highly relevant to LMIC policy on seasonal hunger, internal migration, and rural labor markets; quantifies wage and price effects useful to practitioners. Applicability varies with context and market integration; later scale-up evidence mixed, warranting cautious extrapolation.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Rounded mean of component midpoints. Excellent causal design and scale; strong online evidence and useful policy takeaways. Uncertainty stems from limited offline behavioral results and constraints on data sharing/replication.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Core questions are clear; endorsement and source-citation effects identified causally with platform-specific variation. Offline impacts are framed as suggestive and caveated. Evidence is strong for online diffusion; offline outcomes rely on survey measures with selection and self-report limits.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Large preregistered field experiment; clever identification exploiting Twitter’s author/retweeter visibility. Robustness via forced-retweet randomization and checks on visible engagement counts; appropriate Poisson models and fixed effects. Assumptions reasonable. Limited power for offline behavior; external validity beyond Twitter/users is constrained.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Provides rare causal separation of endorsement vs reach at national scale; shows source citation can hinder diffusion; informs complex contagion shape. High practical and theoretical relevance for social influence and health communication. Offline behavior effects are limited, tempering the ceiling.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Goals, design, and assumptions are explicit; reasoning links evidence to claims cleanly. Figures/tables align with narrative; caveats stated. Dense in places but overall very clear and transparent.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Pre-registered; IRB approved; methods and analyses described in detail. Twitter data likely restricted by TOS; code/data availability not fully open, and platform changes hinder reproduction. Still, procedures are documented enough for credible replication in similar contexts.

label_paper_title: When Celebrities Speak: A Nationwide Twitter Experiment Promoting Vaccination In Indonesia
rationale: Directly relevant to vaccine promotion and public communications in LMICs; offers actionable guidance on influencer use, messaging, sources, and exposure strategy. Quantifies effects useful for campaign design; downstream behavioral evidence is modest.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Strong theoretical contribution plus solid empirical demonstrations; some external-validity and assumption limits temper the score. Results are decision-relevant and clearly communicated. Average across categories reasonably reflects performance; no single metric dominates enough to override the default mean.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Clear questions and claims; theory tightly linked to empirics. Two incentivized RCTs estimate ATEs, heterogeneity, and covariance with bias/externalities. Sensitivity analyses (pass-through, markups, variance/covariance) aid credibility. Limits: cars choices are hypothetical; drinks bias relies on proxies; key independence/normality assumptions; external validity cautions.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Rigorous sufficient-statistic framework with Weyl–Fabinger supply; careful mapping to estimands. Mixed-effects estimation of Var[τ] via dispersion, and targeting via Cov with bias/externalities. Preregistration, incentivization, and extensive sensitivity. Weaknesses: no PAP, normality/independence assumptions, proxy-based bias in drinks, non-naturalistic car choices, literature-based pass-through.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Shifts nudge evaluation from average effects to distortion-variance and targeting; unifies taxes, pass-through, market power, psychic costs. Portable sufficient statistics; dual experiments illustrate feasibility. Likely to influence behavioral public finance and policy appraisal.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Goals and assumptions explicit; derivations and intuition (examples, figures) are clear. Empirical-to-theory mapping is transparent. Caveats and limitations are candid. Minor complexity remains for non-specialists.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: Trials registered (AEA, ClinicalTrials); IRB approvals; replication files posted. Methods sufficiently detailed for reproduction. No full pre-analysis plan; some data access constraints (panel, shipping logistics). Overall, above-average transparency.

label_paper_title: When do Nudges Increase Welfare?
rationale: High policy relevance (labels, sin taxes, nudges) across sectors; guidance on when nudges help or harm welfare, useful for regulators and practitioners. Empirics are US-centric; limited direct cost/practical implementation detail for LMIC contexts, but framework generalizes.

Substantial contribution to innovation economics; some limits to external validity beyond U.S. institutions.

label_paper_title: NA

label_paper_title: NA

label_paper_title: NA

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: Clear statement of the question; precise causal claims focused on LATE; multiple robustness checks (placebos, dynamics, panel corroboration). Evidence convincingly supports increased firm creation. Some residual concerns remain about formalization vs. new entry, compliers’ representativeness, and possible alternative channels.

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: Novel, well-argued running-variable instrument with fuzzy RD/IV; strong first stage; balance and profiling; permutation-based expected instrument; complementary panel DiD. Assumptions (rain exogeneity within week×location, monotonicity, no direct effects) are plausible but nontrivial; administrative matching noise possible.

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: First rigorous estimate (to my knowledge) of legalization’s impact on entrepreneurship in a developing-country context; adds practice-relevant magnitudes and a reusable method. External validity beyond Venezuelans in Colombia is uncertain but the contribution is substantive.

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: Reasoning is transparent; assumptions and design laid out carefully; results tied to claims with clear narrative and figures. Technical sections are dense, which may challenge some readers, but overall argumentation is coherent and consistent.

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: Uses administrative data unlikely to be publicly shareable; methods and appendices are detailed, but no explicit code/data repository is indicated. Replication feasible in principle with access, but practical reproducibility is constrained.

label_paper_title: Legalizing Entrepreneurship
rationale: Highly relevant to migration regularization policies and entrepreneurship in LMICs; produces actionable effect sizes and timing. Findings inform integration strategies and institutional design; generalizability plausible though context-specific factors remain.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Exceptionally strong, policy-relevant RCT with novel UBI design and careful analysis. Major strengths: scale, pre-registration, multiple arms, high compliance, rich outcomes, and clear caveats. Limitations: short time horizon so far, modest power for cross-arm contrasts and prices, some self-reports, and external validity beyond rural Kenya. Overall score equals mean of component midpoints.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Clear questions (UBI vs short-term vs lump-sum), strong multi-source evidence (household, enterprise census, wages, prices), and cautious interpretation. Authors pre-specify aggregates, acknowledge limited power for between-arm two-sided tests and uncertain price effects, and align findings with a simple model without overstating causality on mechanisms.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Large village-level RCT; strong pre-registration; high response and compliance; migrant tracking; Conley SEs; multiple data modules. Sensible specification choices and transparency on limits. Limits: between-arm power constraints, short-run horizon, some self-reported measures, and limited ability to identify general-equilibrium price effects.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: First large UBI RCT with 12-year commitment and cross-arm modality contrasts. Provides rare evidence on structural shifts, occupational choice, enterprise dynamics, mental health, and the importance of tranching and duration. Highly influential for cash-transfer design and understanding savings/credit constraints in LMICs.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Objectives, concepts, and assumptions are explicit; theory-to-empirics link is clear. Writing is thorough and transparent about caveats and inference limits. Tables and figures generally match narrative and are interpretable; minor density/complexity is expected given scope.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Pre-analysis plan registered; IRBs and conflicts disclosed; design and measures well-documented. Replication seems feasible, but public availability of full data/code isn’t clearly established in the text provided; hence a conservative score pending confirmed open materials.

label_paper_title: Universal Basic Income: Short-Term Results from a Long-Term Experiment in Kenya
rationale: Directly relevant to UBI and cash-transfer policy in LMICs under fiscal and administrative constraints. Results inform modality (lump-sum vs streams), duration, and macro spillovers for practitioners. Communication is accessible for policymakers, with quantitative magnitudes and practical implications.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Strengths in clarity and high policy relevance offset by reliance on modeling assumptions, moderate methodological novelty, and limited openness. Overall reflects the mean of sub-scores; decisions hinge on simulated evidence with good sensitivity checks but uncertain replicability.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Main questions and claims are clear: portfolio economics for mRNA EID vaccines are unattractive without public support. Evidence is simulation-based, calibrated to literature and expert input, with extensive sensitivity analyses. Characterization of limitations is generally accurate, though some strong conclusions hinge on uncertain price/demand assumptions.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Monte Carlo framework with correlated trial outcomes, outbreak stochasticity, cost models, and sensitivity analysis is reasonable. The biologically motivated correlation metric is plausible but unvalidated; many parameters are assumed. No preregistration or code shown; no multiple-testing issues but model risk remains. Robustness explored but empirical validation is limited.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Extends prior megafund work by adding mRNA-specific parameters, outbreak-driven cash flows, and clearer cost/revenue drivers (e.g., price-per-dose threshold, clinical cost dominance). Useful for policy design, but advances are incremental and depend on assumptions; limited direct empirical contribution.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Well-structured, transparent about assumptions, clear executive summary and visuals. Reasoning links methods to conclusions coherently; sensitivity analyses support claims. Some parameter choices could use deeper justification, but overall argumentation is easy to follow and consistent.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Parameters are sourced and supplementary materials are referenced, but code/data availability is unclear. Replication would be straightforward with code, yet not evidently provided. No preregistration. Internal consistency appears solid, but openness and reproducibility practices seem limited.

label_paper_title: Accelerating Vaccine Innovation for Emerging Infectious Diseases via Parallel Discovery
rationale: Highly relevant to pandemic preparedness, vaccine financing, and policy tools (AMCs, stockpiles, guarantees). Addresses practical constraints (affordability, cannibalization, trial costs) and offers decision-relevant thresholds. Findings are actionable for governments, funders, and CEPI-like entities.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Well-executed RCT with credible short-term impacts on mental health and skills, strong policy relevance, and clear exposition. Limitations: short follow-up, reliance on self-reports for key outcomes, and modest open-science practices. Percentile reflects balanced strengths across categories.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Main claims are clearly stated and largely supported by experimental evidence and predictive heterogeneity. The two-pathways mechanism is plausible but partly identified; economic outcomes are proxied and short-term. No long-run evidence; several outcomes are self-reported. Strong but not definitive.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Clustered RCT with re-randomization, baseline controls, randomization inference, indices, and LASSO with holdout for heterogeneity—appropriate and transparent. Risks: many outcomes without formal FWER/FDR beyond indices, short horizon, unclear preregistration, and possible reporting bias.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Shows sizeable short-run impacts of group CBT by lay counselors in a general poor population; challenges targeting-only view; introduces predictive vulnerability heterogeneity. Adds to development and global mental health literatures with a practical delivery model. Lacks long-run and cost-effectiveness estimates.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Clear framing and theory (bandwidth, vulnerability), design, and results; limitations and contrast with Kenyan null are discussed. Reasoning is mostly transparent; some mechanistic claims remain interpretive. Presentation appears coherent and consistent.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Manual shared and methods described; RI and LASSO details provided. However, no explicit public posting of data/code or preregistration is indicated, limiting ease of replication and reuse.

label_paper_title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy among Ghanas Rural Poor Is Effective Regardless of Baseline Mental Distress
rationale: Addresses mental health and human capital in a low-income setting with a scalable delivery model (NSS-compatible), showing meaningful short-run gains. High policy salience. Practical usefulness would increase with costs, implementation detail, and durability evidence.

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts

Robustness is discussed qualitatively; little formal sensitivity analysis, preregistration, or multiple-testing correction (mostly not applicable for a guide). Validity hinges on careful interpretation rather than new estimation.

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts
rationale: Synthesizes dispersed concepts into actionable guidance for CEA practitioners, likely improving practice by tempering overinterpretation and misgeneralization. Contribution is primarily integrative and pedagogical; limited novel methodology or parameter estimates.

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts
rationale: Clear structure (summary, key takeaways, guidance, worked example). Concepts defined and reasoning steps explicit; conclusions aligned with presented arguments. Minor quantitative thresholds could use fuller derivations, but overall communication is strong and practitioner-friendly.

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts
rationale: As a conceptual guide, data/code are not central. Citations and reasoning appear transparent; reproducibility of the worked example likely. However, limited provision of reusable code, datasets, or formal replication materials reduces the open-science score.

label_paper_title: Replicability & Generalisability:  A Guide to CEA discounts
rationale: Directly relevant to cost-effectiveness analysis in global health/development and philanthropy. Guidance on discounting noisy evidence and generalization is actionable for analysts and decision-makers, supporting better allocation under uncertainty.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: Arithmetic mean of category midpoints. Strong RCTs with long-run follow-up, robust results on mental health and behavioral updating; transparent nulls on economics. Open-science practices are good but not exemplary.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: Clear questions; two randomized trials with 4–5 year follow-up. Strong, well-powered effects for HAP; transparent nulls for THPP and economic outcomes. Expert-forecast benchmarking adds credibility. Limitations and deviations from PAP are disclosed and minor.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: Credible RCT design; balanced attrition; validated PHQ-9; incentivized tasks; DML controls; multiple-hypothesis corrections; robustness and mediation analyses. Limits: 24–31% attrition, limited power for some outcomes, some modules added post-PAP, external validity constraints.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: Major contribution on long-run psychotherapy impacts in LMICs; cost-effectiveness quantified; novel evidence on belief updating and self-perception; recalibrates expert priors; clarifies limits on economic outcomes, guiding complementary interventions.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: Goals, concepts, and assumptions are clear. Argument flows logically; analyses match claims; nulls and caveats are explicit. Tables/figures are interpretable; consistency across sections is strong.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: IRB, preregistration, and pre-analysis plan; multiple-hypothesis adjustments; expert forecasts via SSPP. Replication seems feasible, but public data/code availability is unclear/limited due to human-subject constraints.

label_paper_title: The Long-Run Effects of Psychotherapy on Depression Beliefs and Economic Outcomes
rationale: High policy relevance for mental health scale-up in LMICs; durable, low-cost effects; quantified cost per depression-month averted. Practical insights on lack of economic gains inform program design and integration with other supports.

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives
rationale: Overall set to the mean of component midpoints. Clear, persuasive synthesis with actionable proposals, but causal evidence is limited and open-science practices are weak. label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives

label_paper_title: Stagnation and Scientific Incentives
rationale: Highly relevant to funders, universities, and policymakers concerned with research productivity worldwide. Recommendations (dual metrics; search engine changes) are actionable, though implementation challenges and cost-benefit quantification are not deeply developed.

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers
rationale: Introduces and operationalizes a non-anthropocentric SWF with representative-agent WTP/WTA for animal welfare, linking to optimal taxation and cross-externality concerns. Provides first-cut estimates and comparisons to prior modeling work. Despite weak empirics, the conceptual framing can stimulate better-designed follow-ups.

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers
rationale: Clear motivation and theoretical setup; assumptions are mostly explicit; limitations and sensitivity are candidly discussed. Some overreach between evidence and conclusions; complex exclusions/outlier handling can confuse. Tables generally align with narrative.

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers
rationale: No preregistration, data, or code availability indicated. Survey instrument only partially reproduced. Outlier and winsorization choices are described but not fully auditable without materials. Replication would be approximate rather than exact.

label_paper_title: The animal welfare cost of meat: evidence from a survey of hypothetical scenarios among Belgian consumers
rationale: Topic (animal welfare externalities, meat taxation, cross-externality trade-offs) is globally salient for policy and prioritization. Findings could inform debates (e.g., chicken vs beef). label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: Main questions are explicit; evidence is strong: nationwide firm-level RCT, cross-randomized intensity, and appeal-level visibility experiment. Effects on violations, emissions, regulator behavior, and ambient SO2 triangulate. Alternative mechanisms probed and largely ruled out. External validity is the main caveat.

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: Well-justified design; preregistered; firm FE, province×day FE, appropriate clustering, event studies, alternative definitions, manipulation checks, and GE design. Appealing identification at scale. Some multiple-testing risk and a few appeal-level analyses are cross-sectional, but overall robustness is high.

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: First experimental evidence at national scale on citizen participation’s direct and indirect effects in environmental governance; identifies regulator responsiveness via social media visibility. Influential for political economy and policy design. Generalizability beyond China is uncertain but insights are substantial.

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: Clear goals, concepts, and transparent reasoning. Results logically support conclusions; figures/tables align with narrative. Length and technical density may limit accessibility for some practitioners, but exposition is careful and accurate.

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: AEA RCT registry and detailed appendices/protocols. However, core administrative data are not fully public; code/materials availability is not fully clear, limiting turnkey replication. Documentation quality is good given constraints.

label_paper_title: Does the Squeaky Wheel Get More Grease? The Direct and Indirect Effects of Citizen Participation on Environmental Governance in China
rationale: High relevance to environmental governance, accountability, and cost-effective compliance tools in LMICs. Actionable insights for regulators/NGOs. Institutional features (CEMS scale, Chinese social media) may limit direct transfer, but principles generalize well.

label_paper_title: Choose Your Moments: [NIH] Peer Review and Scientific Risk Taking
rationale: Overall quality is strong: clear question, careful experimental design, robust analysis, and practical implications. label_paper_title: Choose Your Moments: [NIH] Peer Review and Scientific Risk Taking
rationale: Claims are clear and appropriately bounded: scientists value dissensus (variance), experts more so; bimodality not preferred; tighter budgets reduce tolerance; potential funding reversals. Evidence: two well-powered DCEs with NIH-funded scientists, randomized proposal proximity, multiple robustness checks, and application to external datasets. Main caveats: stated preferences not revealed behavior, selection/response bias, and no preregistration.

label_paper_title: Choose Your Moments: [NIH] Peer Review and Scientific Risk Taking
rationale: Strong DCE design (BIBD), randomized expertise proximity, fixed effects, clustered SEs, multinomial and G-MNL robustness, and placebo/hover checks. Sensible modeling of score moments and heterogeneity.
